title: weave event
description: weave-event v1 — one JSON line per merge, written to stderr by weave-driver behind the `weave-event: ` prefix when WEAVE_EVENT=1 is set. Off by default. A findings document says what one merge did in detail; an event line says what happened, in one row per merge, so a run of thousands can be queried without joining four stderr channels by hand. Every field is a fact the driver already had — the exit code, the entity summary the audit writes, the counts the conflict report prints — so turning the channel on costs one line and no extra work. A line is written for every outcome, including the ones that produced nothing: a channel that only records successes cannot answer why a run went wrong.

schema.description: Which document this is. Consumers should key on the pair (schema, schema_version).

schema_version.description: Semver of THIS schema. Consumers must reject a major they do not know. Adding a field is a minor bump; removing one or changing what it means is a major bump.

weave_version.description: The weave-driver build that wrote the line. On the line rather than inferred from a deployment, because a fleet is rarely on one version and 'which build decided this' is the first question a surprising verdict raises.

outcome.description: What happened, in the same three states as the exit code. `clean` and `conflict` both wrote a usable file; `error` wrote nothing that can be trusted.

exit_code.description: The process exit code, stated rather than left to be inferred from `outcome`. 0 clean, 1 conflict, 2 error.

refusal.description: Present only when outcome=error: which refusal it was, as a stable name. `flag_needs_value | not_enough_arguments | unreadable_input | binary_input | unwritable_output`. All five exit 2, and they are five different problems.

message.description: Present only when outcome=error: the same sentence stderr carries, for a person reading one line rather than querying many.

file.description: The repository path of the file merged, as git supplied it (%P), falling back to the output path.

confidence.description: The merge's own confidence, as `weave check` and the audit report it: very_high | high | medium | conflict.

entities.description: The whole entity summary, not a count of it — the same object the audit document carries under `stats`. Grouping a run by any one of its fields is the reason the line is wide.

conflicts.description: Entities left conflicted, and therefore marker boxes in the output.

warnings.description: Advisory findings on a merge that may still be clean — the `weave-warning:` lines, counted. A clean merge with warnings is a real state.

findings.description: conflicts + warnings: everything about this merge somebody might want to look at.

audit_rows.description: Per-entity decisions recorded. Zero means the file took the line-level route, which no other field states directly.

markers.description: Which conflict marker format the output uses: `enhanced` (weave's, with entity metadata) or `standard` (git-compatible, selected by -l).

line_merge_granted.description: Whether this run was given the `git merge-file` route. False means the merge was a function of its three inputs and nothing else.

max_duplicates.description: The threshold in force for this merge: how often one name may repeat before identity stops meaning anything and the file takes the line-level route.

ms_read.description: Milliseconds spent reading the three inputs.

ms_merge.description: Milliseconds spent in the merge itself — the number a performance question is actually about.

ms_total.description: Milliseconds from process start to the decision, including reads and the write.
